attempts.summary: Created an SSH CA on node1 (/etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca, ed25519), signed node1's ed25519 host public key into /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub (principals: node1, 10.100.247.10, localhost; valid 10y), and configured sshd via /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-host-cert.conf (HostCertificate directive). Diagnosed and fixed an SELinux mislabel (tmp_t instead of sshd_key_t) that silently prevented sshd from loading the cert, then restarted sshd. Verified end-to-end that an SSH client whose known_hosts contains only the CA's public key (`@cert-authority * <ca-pubkey>`, no pinned host key) connects successfully and explicitly reports "Host is known and matches the ED25519-CERT host certificate," while an empty known_hosts file fails — proving trust flows from the CA, not key pinning. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and healthy service state, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until the node returned, confirmed boot_id changed, and re-verified sshd active, the host certificate config intact, and CA-based client trust working post-reboot. All test client keys/known_hosts files were cleaned up afterward.
